html:
Artifacts and context

Exact attachments and authorized resource-associated sources use scoped context IDs. Current read_context requests use a bound Context policy, Unicode character budgets and the returned continuation cursor. The deprecated limit argument still counts bytes within that policy; a missing policy does not select a legacy reader. The tool checks source grants; it cannot turn a guessed ID into access. Result IDs refer to real stored observations, not filenames. Use a filesystem tool to read a file before referring to its execution result.

The attachment and Vision guide explains reader selection, verified Gateway copies, archive members and explicit image observations. Those operations share source grants but have separate format and execution limits.

Source ownership and storage

attachments.py owns body files under native-context/ beside the native run-store path. Each upload gets a fresh context ID, recorded SHA-256, byte size and optional UTF-8 character count, with a 64 MiB upload limit. Identical uploads can have different IDs; this is not content-addressed deduplication. The controller keeps source/grant metadata in RAM with its normal recovery lifecycle; standalone stores use SQL metadata. Body files remain a separate filesystem boundary.

Reading existing metadata requires a live conversation grant. Internal bind and link operations establish ownership during admission or server-authorized sharing; they are different from a model's read request. Task Contract and Task Skill paths initially supply metadata without loading attachment text. Other ingress paths may retain a 512-byte preview. Forks append already-granted inherited sources; copied metadata by itself does not create access.

In the controller, conversation deletion first records durable intent and fences access; grant and body cleanup runs later in the collector. The standalone SQL deletion path releases grants in its transaction and returns unshared source IDs for unlinking after commit. Another conversation grant or retained_reusable keeps the source owned. Upload body creation precedes metadata publication. RAM publication failure removes the new body; the standalone SQL branch can leave an unindexed body if metadata insertion fails. No cross-filesystem transaction is implied.

Resource-associated documents

resource_context_assets.py keeps at most one reference for each of four purposes: OpenAPI specification, API schema, API documentation and reference document. Associations require explicit IDs, an already granted nonsecure upload/artifact and the matching resource revision. They own no new bytes or grants, and replacing an association does not delete its upload.

The model receives a bounded manifest. An unverified resource reports a stale association; a missing grant/body or changed recorded digest reports missing. Only active entries expose readable context IDs. Checks inspect recorded metadata and file length without rereading or rehashing the body, and do not infer links from filenames or automatically preload documentation. Actual text retrieval still passes read_context authorization and capacity checks.

history.py and compaction.py manage bounded conversation context. Compaction keeps source/result references and the current task projection so the model can recover values when authorized evidence remains available. Shortening a model observation does not itself delete artifacts or receipts; their separate retention and access rules still apply.

Attached text reads

context_read_policy.py selects a whole policy in global, conversation, then explicit prompt precedence. The default is a bounded read of at most 12,000 Unicode characters. The positive integer cap has no schema maximum, but the model's input budget still limits a usable page. Full-read mode returns all remaining text from the selected offset and ignores requested amount arguments; it does not preload other attachments.

New requests capture the policy. Resumed and continued work keeps its accepted snapshot. Explicit run-policy edits have revisions and affect later read/decision boundaries; changing the global preference does not silently replace an active run's policy. Automatic tool-result preview settings are a separate live presentation policy, described in context budgeting.

The policy API rejects edits to stopped or terminal runs. Supplying a run revision detects stale edits; omitting it does not require a revision match. Resetting a run restores the policy captured before its first explicit run edit, rather than rereading today's global defaults. Resetting a conversation/global override clears that override. The browser validates positive whole-number limits, disables historical run edits, and keeps prompt overrides as local draft intent until admission.

context_reads.py keeps offsets and cursors in original bytes, while max_characters counts Python Unicode characters, including combining marks individually. Successful read cursors bind the context ID, digest, next byte offset and non-UTF-8 encoding when selected; they are not access grants. Use the returned cursor instead of calculating byte positions from displayed text. A UTF-16 BOM counts toward byte offsets while being omitted from text.

The shared decoder supports UTF-8, UTF-16 little/big endian, Latin-1 and CP1252. Auto selects UTF-8 or BOM-marked UTF-16. UTF-32 auto detection, NUL text, invalid decoding and offsets inside an encoded character fail explicitly; known documents/images/archives require their format-aware readers. In bounded mode, the deprecated byte limit backs up to a boundary in the selected encoding and cannot be combined with max_characters; full mode ignores both amount fields.

The reader loads and checks the source's recorded size and SHA-256 before decoding and slicing it, so a small returned page is not a promise of a small disk read or constant memory use. Source extraction provenance remains visible: reaching the end of an extracted text source does not prove that extraction captured the complete original document.

Admission and model delivery

Page admission builds a temporary, correlated transcript including completed sibling reads and pending placeholders for unfinished siblings. Those placeholders are measurement inputs only; they never become execution receipts. It measures the candidate with tool schemas and the saved execution output reservation, without pruning history or generating a response. The complete joined request still passes normal transport admission before inference.

An attached page that does not fit returns no text, zero returned characters and an explicit capacity error. Remaining input space is estimated after the preserved prompt, rather than reported as the whole model window. Read-result aliases share this helper but currently have a separate rejection-metadata limitation.

The budget-rejection path currently constructs its retry cursor with the default UTF-8 encoding. For a rejected non-UTF-8 page, retry using the explicit original byte offset and selected encoding with a smaller amount; do not treat that error cursor as an encoding-preserving continuation. Successful read cursors retain the actual encoding as described above.

Execution preflight, compaction and context reads reserve output space using the run's saved execution reservation. Provider Default can omit the provider's output limit while smTO still reserves that space internally. An explicit execution limit changes the reservation and the room available for input/history. See context budgeting and output limits.

The UI renders actual output and durable state. It does not rewrite a response into an inferred execution plan, deduplicate exact user values semantically, or decide which domain tool should handle ordinary chat.

The policy and mixed-call contracts are exercised by test_context_read_policy.py and test_context_read_batches.py with scoped temporary sources, scripted responses and deterministic counters. test_durable_resource_context.py checks association ownership, lazy retrieval and shared-file retention; test_memory_control_policy_routes.py checks atomic RAM policy edits, revision conflicts and Stop fences.
